To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pore-size distribution is a key factor for the deformation behaviour of sandy deposits, especially in the case of anthropogenic deposits.
the pore size distribution affects the wetting induced deformations of sandy soils.
the collapse of the sand aggregates during wetting is a possible liquefaction triggering mechanism, which depends on the pore size distribution and the void ratio of the sandy soil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the collapse behaviour of sandy soil deposits with different pore size distributions, which are relevant in the context of liquefaction.
the effect of pore-size distribution (PSD) on the collapse behaviour and liquefaction of anthropogenic sandy deposits.
the development of new constitutive models that can be used to describe the behaviour of sandy soils with different pore size distributions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pore-size distribution is an important factor influencing the deformation behaviour of anthropogenic deposits.
a higher macro-void ratio (i.e. more larger pores) leads to more deformation and a lower matrix void ratio (i.e., more compact pseudo-grains) leads to more deformations.
the collapse of sandy deposits is not only related to the global void ratio, but to the pore-size distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wetting induced deformations in sandy soils are strongly affected by the pore-size distribution.
the collapse behaviour of sandy soil deposits is affected by the pore-size distribution and thus by the formation of larger pores (macro-voids).
the collapse of the pseudo-structure in anthropogenic sandy soil is mainly governed by the pore size and the pore size distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collapse behaviour of sandy soil deposits can be affected by the pore-size distribution.
the collapse behaviour of sandy soils can be significantly influenced by the pore-size distribution.
the collapse of sandy soils can occur in two different modes: (i) collapse of the whole sample due to the wetting induced reduction of the void ratio, and (ii) collapse of the pseudo-aggregates.
